text:
incident-bot: P1 pager triggered — EU (eu-west-1) canary latency spike on /generate (95th > 2s). Pager sent to @sasha-oncall and @ryan-runtime at 2026-03-17T02:12:33Z.

sasha-oncall: Ack, joining. Looking at dashboards now.

ryan-runtime: I can see a clear latency bump starting ~02:09 that aligns with a canary push (tag v1.24.3-canary commit abcdef1). Error rate unchanged.

maggie-infra: Confirmed: 10% of eu-west canaries got the kv-prefetch optimization (PR #4310). No 5xx but tail latency increased.

sasha-oncall: Can we flip the canary off or route traffic away quickly?

ryan-runtime: Flag is routing.canary_enabled. I can toggle it off to stop traffic to canary hosts. Preparing command.

sasha-oncall: Do the kill-switch first; avoid full rollback unless needed.

ryan-runtime: Running flag toggle now

```
# runbook shorthand
$ ./tools/flagctl set routing.canary_enabled false --env=prod --region=eu-west-1
# response: success
```

deploy-bot: flagctl: routing.canary_enabled -> false (eu-west-1) by ryan-runtime at 2026-03-17T02:17:10Z.

maggie-infra: Traffic shifting off the canary. 1m roll window.

sasha-oncall: Observability — any immediate drop?

ryan-runtime: 95th dropped from ~2.3s to ~700ms shortly after. Some hosts show KV cache churn but tail is much improved.

emily-cs: Noting: a small set of EU customers likely experienced slow responses for ~5m. No errors. I'll prep a gentle heads-up for customers on higher SLAs.

sasha-oncall: Root cause hypothesis: kv-prefetch changes altered cache TTL and batching, causing lock contention on certain request shapes.

ryan-runtime: Agree. I want to revert the single commit (abcdef1) and push a hotfix build to canary before promoting. Opening revert PR (#4324). Keep canary routing off while we validate.

deploy-bot: PR #4324 opened by ryan-runtime: revert "kv-prefetch optimizations" (commit abcdef1). CI pending.

maggie-infra: Recommend running patched canary in a different EU AZ with a 1-node ramp to validate tail behavior.

sasha-oncall: emily, hold customer comms unless things change.

emily-cs: Holding. If we see any customer-visible errors or >10% degradation, I'll escalate.

ryan-runtime: CI passed. Merging revert and starting hotfix deploy to canary (v1.24.3-hotfix1).

deploy-bot: Deploy started: v1.24.3-hotfix1 -> canary (eu-west-1) by ryan-runtime at 2026-03-17T02:28:45Z.

maggie-infra: Canary hosts updated. Note: routing flag remains false so production traffic won't hit old faulty code; this is validation only.

sasha-oncall: Plan: validate 10m in canary, then enable 1% canary routing and monitor before larger ramps.

(10m validation window)

ryan-runtime: Hotfix canary metrics look good: 95th ~120ms, stable. Re-enabling canary routing at 1% to sanity-check real traffic.

deploy-bot: flagctl: routing.canary_enabled -> true (eu-west-1) by ryan-runtime at 2026-03-17T02:45:12Z (gradual -> 1%).

sasha-oncall: Watching 1% traffic: no spikes. Increase to 10% over 5m.

(5m ramp)

maggie-infra: 10% ramp healthy; no latency increases or errors.

sasha-oncall: OK to promote the hotfix and schedule full rollout. Logging timeline note for postmortem: canary regression due to kv-prefetch change mitigated by flag kill and single-commit revert + hotfix.

emily-cs: Sending internal summary to affected accounts; no SLO breaches detected, impact limited to elevated tail for small EU cohort.

sasha-oncall: Handoff: I'm on call for another ~40m. If issues surface after 03:00Z, page hana-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-latency

hana-oncall: Copy. I'll pick up at 03:00Z and review notes.

sasha-oncall: Closing thread. Summary: canary rollout with kv-prefetch change caused tail latency spike; mitigation via feature-flag kill-switch, revert PR and hotfix deployed and validated in canary, then promoted. Action items: postmortem within 72h, add extra PR review checklist for cache/ttl changes, consider automated canary tail checks.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (P1 -> resolved) at 2026-03-17T03:05:22Z. Ticket INC-20260317-1123. Please file postmortem within 72h.
